title: Slow Cooker Tomato Lentil Soup
description: A hands-off pantry soup with lentils, tomatoes, carrots, and simple seasoning.
substitutions: Use frozen diced carrots and onions to reduce prep.
Stir in kale instead of spinach.

steps.text: Add lentils, vegetables, broth, and seasonings to the slow cooker.

cookSteps.text: Add 1 1/2 cups rinsed lentils, 1 can diced tomatoes, 2 diced carrots, 1 diced small onion, 6 cups broth, 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 6 hours, until the lentils are tender but not mushy.
If using, stir in 2 cups baby spinach. Cover 3–5 minutes until wilted.

storage: Refrigerate up to 5 days or freeze up to 3 months.

title: Sheet-Pan Paprika Chickpeas & Sweet Potatoes
description: Roasted sweet potatoes and chickpeas with smoky paprika for an easy meatless dinner or side.

ingredients.item: medium sweet potatoes, cut in small cubes

substitutions: Use regular potatoes or butternut squash instead of sweet potatoes.
Use white beans instead of chickpeas; add them for the final 15 minutes so they do not dry out.

steps.text: Heat oven and season sweet potatoes and chickpeas.

cookSteps.text: Heat oven to 425°F. Put 2 cubed sweet potatoes and 1 can drained chickpeas on a sheet pan.
Toss with 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 teaspoon paprika, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Spread into one layer.
Roast 25–30 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the sweet potatoes are tender and browned at the edges.
Serve as-is or add a small spoonful of yogurt or sour cream to each portion.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; reheat in a hot oven or skillet for best texture.

title: Leftover Rice Tuna Patties
description: Crisp little skillet patties that turn leftover rice and canned tuna into a quick meal.
substitutions: Use canned salmon instead of tuna.
Use crushed crackers or breadcrumbs instead of flour if needed.

steps.text: Mix rice, tuna, eggs, cheese, flour, and pepper.
Cook in a lightly oiled skillet until crisp on both sides.

cookSteps.text: Mix 2 cups cold cooked rice, 1 drained can tuna, 2 eggs, 1/2 cup shredded cheddar, 2 tablespoons flour, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.
Divide into 8 small patties and press them firmly so they hold together.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook patties about 3 minutes per side until browned and hot through, working in batches if needed.

storage: Refrigerate cooked patties up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet or toaster oven.

title: Small-Batch Blueberry Cobbler
description: A warm berry dessert with a simple biscuit-style topping, sized for a small baking dish.
substitutions: Use mixed berries or chopped peaches instead of blueberries.
Frozen berries can go in without thawing; add about 5 minutes to baking time if needed.

steps.text: Sweeten berries in a small baking dish.
Mix a quick batter and spoon it over the fruit.

cookSteps.text: Heat oven to 375°F. Put 2 cups blueberries in a small baking dish and toss with 2 tablespoons sugar and 1 teaspoon cornstarch.
In a bowl, mix 1/2 cup flour, 1 tablespoon sugar, and 1 teaspoon baking powder. Stir in 2 tablespoons melted butter and 1/4 cup milk just until combined.
Drop spoonfuls of batter over the berries.
Bake 23–25 minutes until the berries bubble and the topping is golden.

storage: Refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days; reheat gently.
